I think you're probably right about the motherboard, but it's worth testing to be sure. I'd want to try another power supply, if you have a compatible one available. I'd also try switching to onboard graphics, assuming you're currently using a separate video card.

I take it you have checked all hardware connections? If so check all cable connections to the MB (especially the power cables), and even daft things like HDMI connection to GPU out and at the other end into the monitor. Something may have been knocked loose. If you have a modular power supply check the cables at PSU end too.

Failing all that, it's time for the tedious process of testing and ruling out components as you have already done with RAM. Is your MB posting? If not is it giving an error code? If so you need to look it up on Manufacturers website.
